As a Vice President, Program Manager – Innovation & AI Transformation in the  Controls Room team , you will lead cross-functional transformation programs that improve control management outcomes by redesigning workflows and embedding AI and automation where they accelerate impact. The Controls Room, part of Control Management, strengthens existing control functions and develops new ones by monitoring firmwide, risk-based intelligence that empowers the three lines of defense. You will translate opportunities into clear roadmaps with measurable outcomes and run governance from pilot through scale, managing dependencies and escalating where broader alignment is needed. You will design solutions across people, process, operating model, data, and technology while balancing time-to-value with risk and control requirements.

Control Management

Control Managers are responsible for having a deep understanding of the business, its underlying processes and the compliance and operational risk and control environment. Subject matter expertise/innovative tools and technology.

Control Management maintains a strong and consistent control environment across the firm. With Control Managers appointed for each Line of Business, Function and Region, there is a comprehensive coverage and joint accountability model with the business executive that promotes early operational risk identification and assessment, effective design and evaluation of controls and sustainable solutions to mitigate operational risk.

Controls Room

The Controls Room Team within Control Management works collaboratively with other control disciplines and oversees existing control functions as well as the development of new control frameworks, protocols, and tooling solutions. The team’s objective is to empower the three lines of defense with risk-based information to manage their control environment. This is achieved by collecting, analyzing and monitoring firmwide risk-based intelligence into all lines of business and corporate functions.

The Controls Room gathers information from key business and technology partners in order to:

•              Facilitate better decision making and actionable insights across the Firm.

•              Create cost-effective and automated reporting; and

•              Provide views into risk and issues.

- Lead AI-enabled transformation programs across control management processes by embedding AI and automation into defined workflows.

jobs.title: Financial Analysis, Associate – Chase Auto Corporate Development Finance
jobs.description:
Description

The candidate will be a member of the Chase Auto Corporate Development Finance deal team, responsible for modeling deal economics with major auto producers and co-leading negotiations. The Private Label Captive Finance team serves as a planning and analytical resource to help executives manage, forecast, plan, and assess business profitability and new opportunities. We use financial data and recommendations to influence the Auto Leadership Team on the direction to pursue. This includes upside sensitivities showing projected profit if deals perform as expected, as well as downside risk sizing for potential “black swan” events such as economic hardship or car maker specific challenges. We also analyze emerging technologies to identify defensive and offensive opportunities and use these insights to help drive new strategies within Chase Auto.

As an Associate Financial Analysis in the Chase Auto Corporate Development Finance Deal Team, you will evaluate partnership opportunities and support negotiations by modeling economics, risks, and returns. You will help leaders understand expected profitability, key sensitivities, and potential downside outcomes under adverse scenarios. You will partner closely with stakeholders across Pricing, Business, and Credit to align assumptions and translate analysis into decisions. You will communicate findings through executive-ready materials that are clear, concise, and actionable.

You will contribute to business cases that span volume growth, revenue, expenses, and credit losses. You will analyze performance and portfolio trends to inform forecasts and opportunity sizing. You will also support strategic assessments of emerging technologies and market shifts such as identifying opportunities that protect existing business and unlock new sources of revenue. You will operate in a collaborative environment that values curiosity, ownership, and well-supported points of view.

Job responsibilities

- Build and maintain Excel-based financial models to evaluate partnership economics and growth opportunities across the business development lifecycle

- Develop business cases for new initiatives, including assumptions for originations, revenue, expenses, and credit losses

- Perform profitability and income statement analysis to identify performance drivers and inform management decisions

- Conduct sensitivity and scenario analysis to quantify upside potential and downside risk under adverse conditions

- Analyze large historical datasets to identify trends and develop forecasts supporting strategic decision-making

- Develop deep understanding of loan and lease profitability drivers to improve business case quality and rigor

- Partner with cross-functional teams (including Pricing, Business, and Credit) to align inputs, assumptions, and recommendations

- Create clear, executive-ready presentations that communicate complex analysis in a concise and compelling way

- Present findings and recommendations to stakeholders across Finance, Business Development/Sales, and Risk

- Support ongoing monitoring of deal performance and key metrics, escalating insights and risks as appropriate

Required qualifications, capabilities, and skills

- Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, or a closely related field

- 2 + years of experience in financial analysis, corporate finance, or accounting

- Advanced Excel skills, including building structured models and performing scenario/sensitivity analysis

- Experience working with large datasets (extracting, cleaning, and manipulating data to produce insights)

- Ability to translate financial results into clear recommendations and decision-ready summaries

- Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain complex topics clearly

- Experience creating executive-ready materials in PowerPoint (or equivalent presentation tools)

- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, including attention to detail and comfort with ambiguity

- Demonstrated ability to manage multiple priorities and deliver high-quality work under tight deadlines

- Proven ability to collaborate effectively with cross-functional stakeholders

Preferred qualifications, capabilities, and skills

- Experience in consumer lending, auto finance, or another regulated financial services business

- Experience supporting partnership, pricing, or deal-related analyses

- Familiarity with credit loss concepts and risk-adjusted profitability frameworks

- Experience building forecasts and tracking performance to plan (variance analysis)

- Proficiency with SQL, Tableau, Alteryx, or similar analytics tools

- Experience presenting to senior stakeholders and responding to feedback in real time

- Interest in market and technology trends impacting automotive and lending ecosystems

Additional Information

To be eligible for this role, you must be authorized to work in the United States. We do not offer any type of employment-based immigration sponsorship for this role. Likewise, JPMorgan Chase & Co. will not provide any assistance or sign any documentation in support of any other form of immigration sponsorship or benefit, including optional practical training (OPT) or curricular practical training (CPT). This role is not eligible for relocation assistance.


Model partnership economics, build business cases, and deliver insights that shape Chase Auto strategy and profitability.

jobs.title: Private Equity Fund Administration Analyst
jobs.description:
J.P. Morgan’s Finance & Business Management organization is a firmwide function that partners with our businesses and corporate teams to drive financial discipline, transparency, and strategic insight. Our teams deliver end‑to‑end financial control, planning and analysis, forecasting, and management reporting that enable leaders to make informed decisions and maintain resiliency across market cycles. Operating across major global hubs and working closely with Technology, Operations, and Business partners, we build scalable processes, strong controls, and actionable analytics that support the firm’s growth and operational excellence

- Adhere to control framework including internal policies and procedures

- Bachelor’s Degree in Accounting, Finance or related field
- 2+ years’ experience in an accounting role, preferably at a Big 4, PE firm or fund administrator
- Knowledge of US GAAP for Investment Funds and familiar with Private Equity fund structures
- Analytical thinker and problem solver with attention to detail
- Ability to work under pressure and balance multiple priorities
- Team Player with excellent interpersonal, communication and client service skills as well as the ability to see projects to completion
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office product suite and strong MS Excel skills

Preferred qualifications, capabilities, and skills
- Professional accounting qualification (CA, CPA) a plus
- Experience with Investran or similar integrated Private Equity system a plus

jobs.title: Global Corporate Banking - Subsidiary Banking – Intra-Asia Greater China Desk,  Executive Director
jobs.description:
The senior Greater China Desk banker will play a key leadership role within the Intra-Asia Subsidiary Banking franchise, with primary responsibility for driving the growth of our Greater China corporate client business across Asia Pacific region.

The role will focus on deepening relationships with leading Greater China corporates as they expand their business, investments and financial activities across ASEAN and the broader Asia Pacific region. The successful candidate will combine strong senior-client connectivity in Greater China with a deep understanding of cross-border corporate banking, capital allocation, risk management and broader institutional banking product suite.

As a senior member of the Intra-Asia team, the individual will also help shape the strategic direction of the franchise, develop the Greater China coverage team and serve as a senior bench leader capable of taking the Intra-Asia Greater China business to the next level.

Key Responsibilities:

- Lead the Greater China Intra-Asia growth strategy:

- Drive sustainable revenue growth and returns from the Greater China portfolio. Maintain disciplined prioritization of capital and resources, with a strong focus on relationship returns, wallet capture and cross-product penetration.

- Own and drive the strategy for Greater China-headquartered corporates operating and investing across Asia, with particularly focus on ASEAN and other priority platforms such as RTC, RHQ, IHQ in Hong Kong and Singapore corridors.

- Identify structural growth themes and emerging client opportunities arising from Chinese corporates’ regional and global expansion, including manufacturing relocation, supply-chain diversification, energy transition, digital infrastructure, technology, innovation economy and AI infrastructure sectors.

- Translate these themes into actionable client strategies, prioritized prospect pipelines and measurable revenue opportunities.

-
Partner with Greater China and regional leadership to continuously refine the target client universe and resource allocation across the franchise.

- Drive senior client coverage and origination:

- Develop trusted relationships with CFOs, Treasurers and other senior decision-makers at leading Greater China corporates.

- Lead strategic dialogue with clients around their cross-border banking and financing needs, including payments/cash management, liquidity, trade finance, market FX and rates, lending, capital markets and other strategic financing solutions.

- Originate complex, multi-product and multi-country opportunities by connecting clients with the bank’s capabilities across markets and products.

- Act as a senior escalation and relationship point for strategically important Greater China-headquartered clients across Asia Pacific region. Facilitate senior connectivity between Greater China corporate decision-makers and the bank’s regional and global leadership.

-
Build effective coverage models that combine strong headquarters relationships with high-quality subsidiary coverage in destination markets. Coordinate client strategy across countries and products to ensure a consistent, enterprise-wide approach to priority relationships.

- Provide franchise leadership:

- Serve as a senior member of the Intra-Asia leadership team and contribute to broader strategy and management of the franchise.

- Provide leadership, coaching and sponsorship to Greater China Desks bankers and help develop the next generation of senior coverage talents.

-
Raise standards around client planning, origination, execution and senior stakeholder management.

Required Qualifications and Skillsets:

- Bachelor’s degree in Business, Finance, Accounting, Economics, or related discipline.

- Minimum 10 years of relevant corporate banking experience, including coverage of China-linked clients and/or Greater China corridors.

- Significant corporate banking or institutional client coverage experience, ideally including substantial Greater China and cross-border responsibilities. Mandarin proficiency (spoken and written), aligned to client coverage needs.

- Strong understanding of transaction banking, markets, credit, trade finance, and the ability to connect these into cohesive client solutions. Proven relationship management and origination capability, including negotiation and long-term client stewardship.

- Demonstrated experience coordinating complex, multi-product and multi-country opportunities with multiple stakeholders and tight execution timelines. Strong analytical skills and commercial judgment, with the ability to align opportunities to risk appetite and controls.

-
Excellent oral and written communication skills; ability to influence and coordinate across internal stakeholders and client teams. Strong organization skills with ability to manage multiple concurrent deliverables while maintaining execution quality and deadlines.

Preferred Qualifications and Skillsets:

- Familiarity with multinational subsidiary treasury operating models, including cross-border liquidity structures, cash concentration, and intercompany flows.

- Demonstrated leadership capability with a collaborative, team-oriented approach, effectively partnering across coverage and product stakeholders to drive shared objectives and business outcomes.

- Track record of effective partnership with Risk, Compliance, and Credit stakeholders in a high-control environment, including issue escalation and remediation support.


An exciting opportunity to join our GCB SB Team managing China Desk clients!

jobs.title: Artificial Intelligence Research, Business Operations Lead
jobs.description:
JPMorganChase AI Research (AIR) is a global team of research scientists, engineers and product managers that develops novel AI capabilities and partners across the firm to translate breakthrough AI/ML techniques into deployed solutions. The team brings together researchers across multi-agent systems, foundation model training, reinforcement and continual learning, multimodal document AI, formal reasoning, planning and verification, and synthetic data generation – alongside experts in trustworthy AI, privacy, and cryptography – to solve hard problems end-to-end in ways that are secure, reliable, and scalable in financial services.

AI Research sits within the Chief Data & Analytics Office (CDAO) at JPMorganChase which is responsible for accelerating the firm’s data and analytics journey. This includes ensuring the quality, integrity, and security of the firm's data, as well as leveraging this data to generate insights and drive decision-making. The CDAO is also responsible for developing and implementing solutions that support the firm’s commercial goals by harnessing artificial intelligence and machine learning technologies to develop new products, improve productivity, and enhance risk management, effectively and responsibly.

As Business Operations Lead, VP/ED, supporting AI Research, you will be the strategic operating partner to the leadership of one of the most ambitious AI research organizations in financial services. You will shape how the team plans, invests, executes, and scales – aligning talent, capital, and infrastructure behind a bold research agenda. This is a rare seat at the intersection of cutting-edge AI, executive strategy, and enterprise execution – ideal for a leader who thrives on turning ambiguity into structure and enabling brilliant people to do their best work.

Job responsibilities

- Serve as the strategic operating partner and chief of staff to the Head of AI Research, driving execution of the team’s strategy and long-term roadmap.

- Orchestrate executive management reviews, leadership offsites, and deep-dive sessions – shaping the agenda, framing key decisions, and driving follow-through on outcomes.

- Lead portfolio strategy and governance: intake and prioritization of research and line of business initiatives against the highest-value opportunities across the firm.

- Own executive reporting and narrative development – communicating progress, impact, and strategic direction to senior stakeholders across CDAO and the lines of business.

- Steward the financial resources of the team to enable innovation and implementation in a fiscally responsible way – partnering with finance on multi-year planning, headcount strategy, and disciplined allocation across talent, compute, and external commitments.

- Shape the team’s presence at flagship, signature AI/ML conferences – setting a coherent external engagement strategy that elevates the firm’s research brand and talent pipeline.

- Partner with analytical, data, and infrastructure platform teams to unlock the capabilities researchers need – compute, models, tooling, and data – and ensure AI Research’s priorities are represented in enterprise platform roadmaps.

- Champion responsible AI governance and a balanced application of controls – enabling the team to move fast, take smart risks, and innovate within a strong risk and compliance posture.

- Aid the talent strategy and operating fabric of the team – hiring, onboarding, workplace, and culture initiatives that make AI Research a destination for the best researchers in the world.

Required qualifications, capabilities, and skills

- 5+ years of business operations, COO, chief-of-staff, or strategy leadership experience – ideally supporting a research, technology, or highly technical organization.

- Track record as a trusted advisor to senior executives, translating vision into operating plans and driving cross-functional execution.

- Strong financial and commercial acumen – multi-year planning, resource allocation, and stewarding investment in innovation.

- Portfolio and prioritization instincts – able to focus a talented team on the highest-impact work amid many competing demands.

- Excellent written and verbal communication; produces crisp executive narratives, board-ready materials, and clear strategic updates.

- Sound judgment on risk, controls, and governance – with the instinct to balance speed of innovation with responsible execution.

- Highly organized, detail-aware, and outcome-driven, with a bias to action and calm under ambiguity.

- Collaborative operator who builds trust and influence across research, engineering, product, legal, finance, and business partners.

- Genuine curiosity about AI/ML and a passion for the mission of applying frontier research to real-world financial services problems.

- Energized by enabling others – you take pride in making a world-class team even more effective.

Preferred qualifications, capabilities, and skills

- Experience operating inside a large financial services or otherwise regulated environment.

- Familiarity with AI/ML research workflows, top-tier academic conferences, and the publication and IP lifecycle.

- Exposure to technology and infrastructure investment decisions (e.g., compute/cloud economics, platform prioritization, model governance).

- Advanced degree (MBA, MS, or equivalent) in a business, engineering, or quantitative discipline.

You will help our clients solve complex business challenges and achieve their objectives with customized financing solutions, risk management, working capital, cash management, and investments. ·         Initiate and maintain strategic dialogue with DI clients and prospects to generate corporate finance, treasury services and credit opportunities

·         Conduct comprehensive client analysis to identify business needs and deliver concrete financial solutions

·         Manage complex, multi-product client relationships as the primary corporate banking representative

·         Partner closely with Investment Banking coverage and product partners, and coordinate the sales and service efforts of partners across the firm

·         Collaborate with credit underwriting team on analysis, structuring, negotiation, and documentation of credit requests

·         Drive account planning process for clients and prospects, with a particular focus on the use of credit capital and balancing firm wide priorities

·         Minimum of 15 years of experience in corporate banking or investment banking;

·         Strong leadership abilities in business development and transaction execution

·         Solid corporate finance, credit, and problem-solving skills

·         Excellent oral and written communications

·         Knowledge of credit, corporate finance, treasury, investment banking, and other banking products

·         Completion of a recognized bank credit training or investment banking training program

jobs.title: Fraud Manager III- Business Operations
jobs.description:
Advance your career with JPMorganChase’s Merchant Services Fraud organization, where innovation, disciplined execution, and operational excellence come together to strengthen fraud prevention, protect customers, and improve business performance. If you enjoy turning complex data and competing priorities into clear decisions, improving processes at scale, and acting as a trusted advisor to senior leaders, this role offers a high-impact platform to do exactly that—while contributing to best-in-class client protection and a stronger client experience.

As a Merchant Services Fraud Business Management Lead (Vice President), you will serve as a trusted advisor and counterweight to Business/Group Heads—helping shape strategy, optimize performance, and drive strong governance through cross-functional partnership. This is a dynamic, time-pressured, and highly visible role that translates strategic priorities into tangible execution across Merchant Services, coordinating the right resources to deliver outcomes that matter to both the firm and our clients.

You will run core business management cadences and executive communications—owning leadership-ready reporting and presentations and shaping the Merchant Services Fraud narrative for senior leadership updates and global town halls. You will lead performance management across KPI/KRI, scorecards, and OKRs, delivering rigorous insights, variance analysis, and escalation of emerging risks and trends to enable timely decisions. You will track strategic investments and initiatives through to delivery, support budget management from internal work rates through case-level budget oversight aligned to the capacity model, and partner closely with Finance, Technology, Operations, Legal, and Compliance to align priorities, resolve blockers, and strengthen end-to-end execution.

In addition, you will help elevate how we deliver fraud detection, prevention, and remediation outcomes by improving the operating model, governance routines, and tool enablement that support teams managing complex situations and customer expectations. You will also govern “single source of truth” repositories and enabling tools, driving continuous improvement and automation to reduce manual effort and operational risk—while supporting a culture focused on excellence, client satisfaction, and ongoing development.

Job Responsibilities

- Lead business management cadences and executive communications (including the MS Fraud narrative): Run business reviews, executive reporting, leadership meetings, and planning/offsite events; produce leadership-ready materials across weekly/monthly/quarterly rhythms (e.g., MBR decks including Senior Leadership versions, weekly inventory slides, quarterly accomplishments) with clear narratives, decisions, and actions; craft and deliver a consistent, data-backed Merchant Services Fraud narrative for leadership updates and global town halls.

- Own performance management and reporting governance: Own KPI/KRI, scorecards, and monthly metrics reporting end-to-end (definitions, data integrity/validation, refresh cadence, variance analysis), including quarterly KRI updates and clear escalation of trends, outliers, and emerging issues.

- Support budget management tied to capacity planning : Partner with Finance and business leads to support budget management from internal work rates through case-level budget tracking, ensuring financial inputs align to (and inform) the capacity model and delivery plans.

- Drive strategy execution, OKRs, and investment tracking: Lead OKR development and governance (setting, accountability, progress visibility) and track strategic investment proposals and delivery against approved plans, milestones, and decisions via transparent status/decision logs.

- Deliver data-driven insights that improve outcomes: Translate data and stakeholder input into actionable recommendations that improve productivity, operating effectiveness, cost/efficiency, and overall bottom-line performance.

- Enable cross-functional alignment and end-to-end delivery: Drive a product-centric operating approach across the full lifecycle (strategy, delivery, adoption, and outcomes) by partnering with key stakeholders and functional partners (Finance, Tech, Ops, Legal, Compliance) to clarify ownership, align priorities, and resolve blockers.

- Own key operational infrastructure and tooling: Govern “single source of truth” repositories (SharePoint/shared drives—structure, permissions, version control, content hygiene) and provide business ownership for user tools and reporting assets (including BRDs), driving technology enhancements and automation in partnership with Tech.

- Manage operational readiness, resiliency, and risk/compliance activities: Define future operational support plans and ownership; conduct horizon scanning to inform leadership of emerging trends and implications; lead business resiliency planning; continuously improve manual exception processes; and coordinate required governance/affirmations and recertifications (e.g., DART evergreen affirmations, IRM recertification, IAS oversight) while identifying, escalating, and mitigating business risks (legal/regulatory, capacity, extraordinary costs).

Required Qualifications, Capabilities, and Skills

- Education: Bachelor’s degree in Business, Finance, Economics, or a related field (or equivalent experience).

- Domain / role experience: Prior Business Management experience and/or strong product knowledge in Merchant Services, ideally in a matrixed, cross-functional environment.

- Business analysis & data discipline (5+ years overall experience): 5+ years of overall experience with demonstrated business-analysis capability—data collection, validation and integrity checks, requirements definition, effective utilization of data, and clear synthesis into decision-oriented insights and reporting.

- Program / project management: Excellent organizational and project management skills; able to manage multiple workstreams with strong attention to detail and a structured, logical approach.

- Strategic ownership & delivery: Ability to define a strategic agenda spanning multiple groups and drive it through to completion, including alignment, execution, and measurable outcomes.

- Stakeholder management & executive presence: Proven ability to build strong internal relationships across a broad set of functions and communicate effectively with senior and global business leaders.

- Communication: Excellent written and verbal communication skills; able to create crisp narratives and present complex topics clearly.

- Tools / technical capability: Strong Microsoft PowerPoint and Microsoft Excel skills, including the ability to build executive-ready presentations and perform quantitative analysis and reporting.

Preferred Qualifications, Skills and Capabilities:

- Relevant functional experience: Experience in business management, operations, project management, and/or business strategy roles.

- Industry experience: Preferred experience in merchant acquiring/processing; broader exposure to payments and/or financial services is also acceptable.

- Strategic orientation: Strategic mindset with the ability to anticipate future demands, challenges, and tradeoffs, and translate them into actionable plans.

- Continuous improvement: Ability to evaluate, refine, and standardize management processes; adapt to emerging threats and trends while maintaining operating efficiency.

- Facilitation & alignment: Ability to facilitate meetings and multi-stakeholder dialogues to drive alignment, decisions, and follow-through.

- Network building: Experience building and expanding business management networks/communities to share best practices and improve consistency across teams.

- OKR familiarity: Familiarity with Objectives and Key Results (OKR) frameworks (goal-setting and progress tracking).

- Growth mindset: Focus on self-development and continuous learning.

- Working style: Energetic and dynamic; highly motivated self-starter with excellent time management and prioritization skills.

- Collaborative, positive, and inclusive team approach: Brings a consistently positive, solutions-oriented mindset; partners exceptionally well across teams; and fosters a welcoming environment by prioritizing the best outcome over ownership championing strong ideas regardless of where they originate.

Global Technology Controller provide controllership support to technology function in to Hardware, Software, Professional services and other direct expense lines. Team is also responsible for capitalization of tangible or intangible assets.

- Validate operational impacts and future benefit assumptions with Technology and business stakeholders and record entries accurately and timely in the general ledger.
- Ensure balance sheet positions are appropriately supported to maintain a strong fortress balance sheet.
- Document analytics through estimates, walk-forwards, controller financial reviews, and flash reports.
- Analyze, communicate, and resolve material variances between the general ledger and upstream systems, as defined by the line of business.

- 3 years of related experience
- General Ledger experience. Experience with financial reporting and month end close responsibilities
- Comfortable liaising with business and risk managers
- Able to build and maintain partnerships within the various product aligned businesses and across other corporate financial, treasury, and accounting groups

- Able to multi-task in a constantly changing environment

jobs.description:
About J.P. Morgan’s Corporate & Investment Bank

J.P. Morgan’s Corporate & Investment Bank (CIB) is a global leader across banking, markets and investor services. The world’s most important corporations, governments and institutions entrust us with their business in more than 100 countries. We deliver strategic advice and solutions for capital raising, risk management and liquidity across global markets.

J.P. Morgan is the global leader in Liability Management. Sitting within Debt Capital Markets, the Liability Management team is responsible for originating, structuring and executing transactions which enable issuers to restructure, or retire, debt obligations as business strategies, objectives and market conditions evolve. The team advises both corporate and financial sponsor clients across the ratings spectrum on their debt capital structure in the context of M&A, leveraged buyouts, refinancings, debt load management, covenant amendments, stressed/distressed situations and balance sheet optimization. The team executes these strategies via tender offers, exchange offers, consent solicitations and debt buybacks. Additionally, we partner with various teams across the investment bank, including capital markets, corporate finance, sales and trading and M&A to provide clients with comprehensive solutions.
This role is for an Analyst in the Liability Management team.
Overview of responsibilities:
- Assist with creating pitch materials

- Monitor liability management opportunities for clients

- Drive processes relating to the origination, structuring and execution of liability management transactions

- Interact with multiple parts of the bank, as well as external parties such as issuers (C-suite and Treasury teams), counsels and third-party agents

- Review and analyze bond indentures and legal documentation associated with liability management transactions

- Build quantitative debt liability management models and maintain key materials such as databases

- Develop a deep understanding of factors (NPV, break-even, maturity profile management, covenant impact, accounting and tax impact, credit rating impact, bondholder composition, etc.) driving corporate finance decision-making

- Develop specific knowledge of the various liability management tools available to issuers

- Strong financial modeling, finance, quantitative and business writing skills

- Comfortable working in a high-pressure environment, possessing superior organizational skills and ability to efficiently multi-task across various deliverables

- Experience with debt products / bond math is a plus

Analysts function as fully integrated team members, in a flat structure that allows for direct client interaction and working directly with MDs, EDs, VPs, and Associates.

- Strong financial modeling, finance, quantitative and business writing skills

- A well-rounded academic background from a top tier educational institution

- Impeccable communication skills with ability to effectively interact with senior professionals, clients and key stakeholders in other lines of business

- Comfortable working in a high-pressure environment, possessing superior organizational skills and ability to efficiently multi-task across various deliverables

- Experience with debt products / bond math is a plus

jobs.description:

·          Take part in origination and execution of ECM transactions led by J.P. Morgan

·          Draft equity market updates to corporate clients on a regular basis leveraging internal and external databases (Bloomberg, Dealogic)

·          Liaise with equity syndicate / research / sales / trading teams in order to gather market intelligence on an ad hoc basis

·          Conduct investor targeting exercises and collect investor feedback using a variety of sources and internal teams (sales / syndicate / research / corporate access)

·          Work together with corporate clients and transaction lawyers

·          At least one year experience in Equity Capital Markets

·          Excellent academic credentials

·          Ability to multi-task, organized, rigorous

·          Interest in capital markets and corporate finance

·          Ability to work within a team, in a fast-moving, results-driven environment

·          Ability to effectively interact with sales people and research analysts, as well as corporate clients and other banks as part of working groups on projects

·          Ability to work independently and to take initiative

·          Proficient quantitative and analytical skills, including PowerPoint and Excel skills

·          Excellent written and verbal communication skills

This role encompasses the performance of regulated activity. The successful candidate will therefore be subject to meeting regulatory requirements in the assessment of fitness, propriety, knowledge and competence (as assessed by the Firm) and (where appropriate) approval by the relevant regulatory authorities to carry out such activities.


This is an exciting opportunity for someone who is highly motivated to work in a dynamic team and to contribute to our Investment Banking business.

jobs.title: Investment Banking - Equity Capital Markets - Analyst
jobs.description:
Job Description

We are seeking an Investment Banking Analyst to join our Equity Capital Markets team, offering an exceptional opportunity to contribute to high-profile transactions and drive growth within a leading capital markets franchise.

Job Summary

As an Analyst in our Equity Capital Markets (“ECM”) team, you will be a key player in driving our platform’s growth and execution. You will participate in the "full cycle" of transaction execution including preparing marketing materials, reviewing and formulating financial analyses, presenting both internally and externally to clients, and driving day-to-day transaction execution. You will experience training, hands-on learning opportunities, continuous mentoring and feedback, and numerous development opportunities. You will use your related experience to contribute to the firm's capital raising capabilities while helping build J.P. Morgan's franchise and reputation in the marketplace. Joining here means you’ll become part of our inclusive teams and culture, unified by the firm’s mission and commitment to success. You will join the global Analyst class within ECM, working with a broader team of over 100 Analysts and Associates in the region on real-time transactions that may include frequent travel.

Job Responsibilities

- Execute public capital raising transactions for issuer clients, including IPOs and follow-on offerings.

- Assist senior bankers in preparation for client engagement, such as pitches and RFPs.

- Liaise with other internal teams including industry coverage, sales and trading, syndicate, equity research and legal.

- Prepare thought pieces related to the equity capital markets and technology sector.

- Drive analysis for issuer clients, including precedent transactions and shareholder targeting.

- Draft presentation materials and internal committee memorandums in advance of launching transactions.

Required qualifications, capabilities, and skills

- Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Economics, Finance or related field.

- Strong accounting, finance, quantitative and business writing skills.

- Knowledge of capital markets and the ECM execution function.

- Impeccable communication skills with the ability to effectively interact with senior professionals, clients and key stakeholders in other line of business.

- Ability to work well in a fast paced, team environment.

- Self-directed, highly motivated, and able to work independently and accurately across multiple ongoing executions and projects.


We are seeking an Investment Banking Analyst to join our Equity Capital Markets team.

jobs.title: Corporate & Investment Banking Credit Risk Analyst
jobs.description:
Are you looking for an exciting opportunity to join a dynamic and growing team in a fast paced and challenging area? This is a unique opportunity for you to work in our team to partner with the Business to provide a comprehensive view.
As a Wholesale Credit Risk APAC – Analyst in the Wholesale Credit Risk APAC team, you will be based in Mumbai playing a crucial role in onboarding new clients, performing credit analysis, structuring, negotiating, and developing recommendations for new transaction approvals across a variety of products, including loans, derivatives, and treasury products. You will lead due diligence and credit analysis to assess the creditworthiness of counterparties, making recommendations on appropriate structures, risk appetite, and client grading. Your role will involve ongoing credit risk portfolio management, new client onboardings, portfolio reviews and ad-hoc macro environment related stress exercises. You will also be committed to personal development and fostering team knowledge by coaching and training members of the Analyst community. Your ability to balance a commercial mindset with a sound risk and controls attitude will be key to managing the Firm’s balance sheet effectively.
Job responsibilities
- Demonstrate proactive ownership of your assigned portfolio of clients including borrower/market performance and acting as the main point of contact for all internal and external stakeholders for your portfolio
- Conduct transaction due diligence and credit analysis to assess counterparty creditworthiness
- Make recommendations on appropriate structure, risk appetite, and client grading informed by forward-looking credit analysis
- Participate in structuring and documentation negotiations with the support of senior colleagues
- Balance a commercial and solution-driven mindset with a sound risk and controls attitude
- Commit to personal development and foster team knowledge through coaching and training
- Develop close working relationships with various stakeholders/product partners within the Commercial & Investment Bank
- Drive key initiatives and process changes by identifying limitations/gaps in systems, risk controls, and policies

Required qualifications, capabilities, and skills
- Bachelor’s Degree in Business, Finance, or a related field
- Familiarity with the concepts of Credit Risk – how it may arise and potential mitigants
- Good interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to establish credibility and trust with internal business and risk stakeholders
- Ability to demonstrate good time management and clarity in thinking when dealing with multiple work streams in a fast-paced environment
- Ability to think holistically and logically and communicate own views in an easy to understand fashion

Preferred qualifications, capabilities, and skills
- 2-3 years of experience in credit risk management in the financial services industry would be highly regarded
- Relevant postgraduate qualifications (e.g., MBA, Masters of Finance, CFA, CA) would be highly regarded
- Knowledge of the Corporates and Financial Institutions financial analysis

jobs.title: Investment Banking – EMEA Healthcare Associate – London
jobs.description:
Description

This is an exciting opportunity for someone who is highly motivated to work in a dynamic team and to contribute to our Investment Banking business.

J.P. Morgan's Investment Banking Healthcare Coverage Group provides a full range of investment banking services to numerous clients based across the EMEA region. Its clients include many of the world's leading firms in their respective industries. The Group's primary focus is on delivering creative solutions to clients for mergers and acquisitions and equity and debt capital raising.

As an Associate in the Investment Banking EMEA Healthcare team, you will be a key player in our business strategy and execution. You will participate in the "full cycle" of transactional execution including preparing marketing pitches, reviewing and formulating financial models and analysis, preparing and presenting internal committee memoranda and client presentations. You will play a leadership role in implementing the execution function including working with other analysts and associates, as well as collaborating closely with senior bankers. You will also have plenty of opportunities to partner with other bankers from the group as well as colleagues from other industry and product teams across EMEA and globally. Joining here means you’ll become part of our inclusive teams and culture, unified by the firm’s mission and commitment to success.

Job responsibilities

-
Project co-ordination, including client communication, co-ordination of advisory team externally and within the bank

-
Develop content for strategic meetings with clients regarding M&A or capital market transactions

-
Conduct detailed valuation analysis and other financial analysis, including DCF, trading comparables, transaction comparables, LBO analysis and transaction structuring

-
Prepare presentation books, management presentations, Board materials, Memorandums, and other presentation materials for use in corporate finance transactions or strategic client dialogue

-
Conduct daily deal execution and project management and take leadership in supporting client coverage by maintaining regular dialogue with clients and potential clients

-
Interact with senior team members and client management teams on a daily basis to execute transactions and discuss strategic alternatives

-
Liaise with J.P. Morgan product teams and global sector teams along with UK equities and research departments

Required qualifications, capabilities and skills

-
Prior investment banking experience, preferably in a Healthcare coverage role

-
Proficient financial modelling / valuation / analytical / numeracy skills

-
Ability to react well to pressure whilst multitasking on numerous projects

-
Ability to comfortably interact with clients in a professional and mature manner

-
High level of attention to detail, proactivity and time management

-
Comfort in and commitment to an inclusive teamwork environment

-
Ability to comfortably interact with people in a professional and mature manner

-
Highly organised, detail oriented and proactive

-
Exceptional written and verbal communication skills with specific ability to communicate concepts and ideas concisely and defend their validity

The successful candidate will therefore be subject to meeting regulatory requirements in the assessment of fitness, propriety, knowledge and competence (as assessed by the Firm) and (where appropriate) approval by the relevant regulatory authorities to carry out such activities.

jobs.title: Investment Banking – Private Capital Advisory – Associate
jobs.description:
Job Summary

We are seeking a highly motivated Associate to join our North American Private Capital Advisory team within M&A and the global Private Capital Advisory & Solutions team. The team advises corporates, sponsors, and privately held businesses on minority investments, joint ventures, and other non-control private capital transactions. These transactions support strategic and financial objectives such as acquisitions, capital investment, growth, monetization, and balance sheet optimization. Working across sectors and alongside industry coverage and product teams, we originate, structure, and execute tailored transactions, including common equity, preferred equity, structured minority investments, and joint ventures. The role is well suited to candidates with experience in structured equity, project finance, infrastructure finance, structured finance, M&A, private equity, or related investing and advisory roles.

Job Responsibilities

- Work with senior bankers and industry teams to originate, structure, and execute minority investments, joint ventures, and other private capital transactions

- Develop financial models and analyses to evaluate transaction structures, cash flows, investor returns, and client outcomes

- Assess how key structural terms, including IRR caps, distributions, leverage, tenor, call rights, and downside protections, affect risk and return

- Support the development and negotiation of transaction terms, including economic, governance, and investor protection provisions

- Prepare client presentations, transaction marketing materials, financial analyses, process materials, and term sheets

- Evaluate potential capital partners and support investor outreach across private equity, infrastructure funds, pension funds, sovereign wealth funds, insurance companies, credit investors, and other institutional investors

- Analyze and compare investor proposals, including return requirements, funding commitments, governance rights, and other material terms

- Coordinate transaction execution from preparation and launch through diligence, negotiation, and signing

- Work with clients, investors, lawyers, accountants, and other advisors throughout the transaction process

jobs.title: Tech Senior Auditor - Commercial & Investment Banking
jobs.description:
We are on the lookout for a talented Senior Associate to join our Commercial Investment Banking Internal Audit team. This is your opportunity to play a crucial role in enhancing our organization's governance and operational excellence!

As a Technology Senior Internal Audit Associate within the Commercial Investment Banking Internal Audit Team, you will execute the annual audit plan, participate in audit engagements by performing audit testing, and participate in various continuous monitoring efforts.

Job Responsibilities

- Participate on technology audit engagements, from planning to reporting, and produce quality deliverables to both department and professional standards, while ensuring audits are completed timely and within budget.

- Work closely with global Audit colleagues in the early identification of emerging control issues, and report them in a timely manner to Audit management and business stakeholders

- Partner with stakeholders, business management, other control groups (i.e. risk management, compliance, fraud prevention), external auditors, and regulators, establishing strong working relationships while maintaining independence

- Finalize audit findings and use judgment to provide an overall opinion on the control environment by developing recommendations to strengthen internal controls

- Communicate audit findings to management, and identify opportunities for improvement in the design and effectiveness of key controls

- Stay up-to-date with evolving industry/regulatory changes impacting the business and participate in appropriate control forums

- Find ways to drive efficiency with existing technical infrastructure through automation while embracing the innovative opportunities offered by new technologies

- Recognize the confidential nature of Internal Audit communications and access to information; exercise discipline in protecting the confidentiality and security of information in accordance with firm policy

Required Qualifications, Skills and Capabilities

- Bachelor's degree in Technology (or relevant experience)

- Extensive internal or external technology auditing experience, or relevant technology risk and control management experience.

- Understanding of internal control concepts, with proven ability to evaluate and determine the adequacy of controls by considering business and technology risks in an integrated manner.

- Strong analytical skills, particularly in regard to assessing the probability and impact of an internal control weakness

- Excellent written, verbal, and presentation skills; adept at presenting complex and sensitive issues to senior management and strong interpersonal and influencing skills, with the ability to establish credibility and build partnerships with senior business and control partners

- Enthusiastic and self-motivated, with a keen interest in learning; effective under pressure and willing to take personal responsibility/accountability as well as flexible to changing business priorities and ability to multitask in a constantly changing environment

Preferred Qualifications, Skills and Capabilities

- Experience with internal audit methodology and applying concepts in audit delivery and execution preferred

- Certified in CISA, CISM, CRISC, CISSP, CCSP or other technology certifications

- Risk management knowledge in public cloud provider (AWS, GCP, Azure) services

To be eligible for this role, you must be authorized to work in the United States. We do not offer any type of employment-based immigration sponsorship for this role. Likewise, JPMorgan Chase & Co. will not provide any assistance or sign any documentation in support of any other form of immigration sponsorship or benefit, including optional practical training (OPT) or curricular practical training (CPT).

jobs.title: Investment Banking - Infrastructure Finance and Advisory - Associate
jobs.description:
We are seeking a highly skilled Associate to join our dynamic Infrastructure Finance & Advisory team.

As an Associate in Infrastructure Finance and Advisory, you'll be joining a team that originates, structures and executes infrastructure finance transactions in developed and emerging markets. The team’s coverage is global, with New York-based members focusing primarily on the Americas. We finance greenfield and brownfield projects across a variety of sectors including transportation, energy, power, telecommunications and social infrastructure as well as acquisition financing in these sectors. Team members have backgrounds in project finance, emerging markets, structured finance and commodities, and we invariably work with colleagues in M&A advisory, debt capital markets, derivatives structuring and other coverage and product groups. By leveraging expertise across products, sectors and markets, the Infrastructure Finance and Advisory team integrates and customizes offerings and solutions to help our clients meet their strategic, financial and risk management objectives.

Job Responsibilities

- Work with senior bankers in originating, structuring and executing infrastructure financing and advisory transactions across various financial products including loans, bonds and structured products

- Support senior bankers with the negotiation of transaction documentation

- Develop financial models and complete financial analyses for infrastructure projects across all sectors

- Work on drafting financing proposals, investor materials, road show marketing materials, rating agency presentations, pitch books and other marketing materials

- Assist in completing transaction due diligence with advisors

- Work with JPMorgan credit risk and legal teams to review transactions in connection with credit risk and other approval processes

- Support senior bankers in answering investor and rating agency inquiries

- Conduct industry and company research to identify new opportunities

Required Qualifications, Capabilities, and Skills

- 4-6 years of investment banking or private equity experience required, preferably with infrastructure/project finance experience

- Bachelor’s Degree required, preferably in accounting, finance, economics or a related field

- Strong quantitative and financial analysis skills required

- Must have significant experience developing project finance models with Excel

- Previous experience creating marketing materials and presentations in PowerPoint

- Must be a self-starter and proactive by taking initiative and anticipating deal team needs

- Willingness to work hard and be a team player. We work closely with partners in banking, capital markets, credit, and various product groups, as well as our partners across the control functions

- An ability to juggle multiple deliverables for long-term transactions as well as a busy day-to-day schedule

jobs.title: Investment Banking – EMEA Energy – Vice President – London
jobs.description:
This is an exciting opportunity for a highly motivated banker to join a dynamic team and contribute meaningfully to our Investment Banking franchise.

Our EMEA Energy team originates and executes public and private M&A and capital markets transactions for corporate and financial sponsor clients across the oil and gas value chain, and our EMEA Energy franchise has been consistently No. 1 ranked. We maintain deep relationships with leading companies and investors across subsectors including Integrated Energy, Upstream, Downstream, Energy Transition including low carbon molecules, Energy Tech, Trading and Marketing, and Petrochemicals, and Energy Infrastructure (e.g., storage, pipelines).

The Energy team is part of our broader Natural Resources platform spanning Energy, Power, Renewables and Mining, and we work jointly with the Power and Renewables team on many clients and projects.

Role overview
As a Vice President in the EMEA Energy coverage team, you will lead day‑to‑day execution on live transactions and play a key role in client coverage and origination. You will manage analysts and associates, partner closely with senior bankers, and collaborate with cross‑border colleagues and product teams (M&A, ECM, DCM, LevFin, Ratings/Credit) to deliver best‑in‑class advice.

Key responsibilities

- Lead and manage the origination and execution of complex M&A and capital markets transactions (buy‑side, sell‑side, take‑privates, carve‑outs, JVs; where relevant, asset/portfolio sales and farm‑in/farm‑out processes).

- Oversee and review financial analysis, valuation and modelling (DCF, trading and transaction comps, merger models, LBOs, accretion/dilution), ensuring analytical rigour and accuracy.

- Develop and present strategic advice and materials to clients, including board‑level executives; contribute to idea generation and pipeline development aligned to EMEA Energy themes.

- Coordinate workstreams with internal product partners and external advisers (legal, accounting, technical and commercial diligence providers) across jurisdictions.

- Drive marketing initiatives, pitches and thought leadership tailored to Energy subsector dynamics, commodity trends and regulatory developments.

- Mentor and develop junior team members; set quality standards, provide training and feedback; support recruiting activities.

- Ensure high‑quality deliverables, strong client relationships and adherence to internal risk, conduct and compliance requirements.

Required qualifications, capabilities and skills

- Significant Investment Banking experience with a strong track record in Energy across products.

- Proven project leadership and process management skills; ability to run multiple cross‑border transactions under tight timelines.

- Advanced quantitative and analytical abilities, including expert Excel modelling and valuation.

- Demonstrated origination contribution (idea generation, relationship development, pitch leadership) and an ability to convert opportunities.

- Excellent interpersonal, written and verbal communication skills; ability to convey complex concepts clearly and defend recommendations.

- Proactive ownership mindset; highly organised, detail‑oriented and decisive.

- Bachelor’s degree or equivalent required; advanced degree a plus.

Preferred qualifications, capabilities and skills

- Additional European language skills.

- Experience with financial sponsors and energy infrastructure investors active in EMEA.

- Familiarity with commodity markets, regulatory frameworks and technical/commercial diligence topics relevant to Energy.

jobs.title: External Reporting Controller, Vice President - Commercial Investment Banking
jobs.description:
The Commercial Investment Banking External Reporting team provides control and oversight to deliver accurate, timely external reporting, including SEC filings and key regulatory reports. The team also leads implementation of new reporting requirements and strengthens the overall control environment.

As an External Reporting Controller, Vice President on the Commercial Investment Banking Team, you will be the lead for governance of Issues & Errors that affect external reporting and will drive the lifecycle from identification through closure, ensuring issues are assessed, escalated, remediated, and prevented from recurring. A key piece of this is the change agenda to leverage AI to streamline the end to end process to be able to quickly identify where the impacts are.

You will also support the quarter end close and analytical review activities to enable confident sign-off of Commercial Investment Banking results included in disclosures and regulatory reports, while leading targeted change initiatives to improve process and control effectiveness.

Job responsibilities

•    Own the end-to-end lifecycle for issues and errors affecting external reporting, from identification through closure, with clear and auditable documentation.

•    Coordinate issue assessment, escalation, and remediation across stakeholders to ensure timely decisions and durable closure.

•    Partner with issue owners to evaluate cross-report impacts, perform pervasiveness assessments, and align on root cause and corrective/preventive actions.

•    Deliver concise, actionable updates to senior leadership on status, risks, and remediation progress.

•    Drive enhancements to the issues and errors operating model, including workflow streamlining, documentation automation, and improved recurrence-prevention practices.

•    Prepare, review, and support earnings deliverables, external reporting, and key regulatory filings through the quarter-end close process.

•    Develop variance and attribution narratives and challenge inputs, assumptions, and judgments impacting reported results.

•    Lead stakeholder forums to align on key developments, reporting risks, and standards changes, including overseeing attestations and related activities.

•    Lead change initiatives and strategic projects (e.g., new rule implementation, process enhancements), with clear scope, milestones, and outcomes.

•    Manage and develop an onshore and offshore team to deliver against reporting, governance, and change objectives.

Required qualifications, capabilities and skills

•    Bachelor’s degree in Accounting or Finance.

•    Minimum 8 years of controllership experience within financial services (e.g., external reporting, product control, financial control, legal entity control, or financial planning and analysis).

•    Strong understanding of markets and banking products, business models, and accounting concepts, gained in a global investment bank and/or professional services environment.

•    Proven people leadership experience, including effective remote management of an offshore team.

•    Strong analytical, problem-solving, organizational, and time-management skills, with excellent written and verbal communication.

•    Demonstrated critical thinking and the ability to challenge established approaches to improve outcomes.

Preferred qualifications, capabilities and skills

•    Certified Public Accountant (CPA) designation (or equivalent).

•    Experience with Databricks, SQL, or similar tools for data extraction and processing.

•    Experience supporting earnings deliverables, SEC filings (10-K/10-Q), and regulatory filings, including FR Y-9C and the Call Report.

•    Track record of driving efficiency through standardization, automation, and responsible use of AI-enabled tools to improve operating cadence, accelerate analysis, and strengthen controls

jobs.title: Investment Banking - EMEA Private Capital M&A - Associate - London
jobs.description:
The Private Capital M&A team sits within EMEA M&A and is part of the global Private Capital Advisory & Solutions team and assists clients raise non-control private capital for a variety of purposes including: M&A, growth/capex, shareholder monetisations, balance sheet equitizations, refinancings etc. The team works closely with country, industry, and other product teams within the bank. The client universe includes large EMEA corporates, sponsor-owned companies and entrepreneur-led / family businesses, who are entering private transactions, including as an alternative to the public market. Capital is raised through bespoke M&A-style processes and from a variety of sources including private equity funds, sovereign wealth funds, alternative & credit investors, pension funds & insurance companies, family offices, and other institutional investors. Private investors are increasingly seeking opportunities to deploy solutions-focused capital and form long-term partnerships with corporates / entrepreneurs. You will get exposure to all sectors, regions, and types of transactions across the capital structure from common equity transactions to more structured deals depending on client requirements.

The team has raised more than $70bn of capital for clients in the last 5 years in over 30 transactions across EMEA. This includes the largest private capital transaction in EMEA in 4 out of the last 5 years, and landmark transactions and partnerships between companies and private investors.

Job responsibilities

- Work with clients in tandem with industry / country teams to analyse the optimal transaction structure and financial modelling for a potential transaction

- Analyse the most suitable investor universe for each transaction and speak to investors as part of the outreach process, be it for bilateral partnerships or broader partner identifications, as well as speaking to investors on an ongoing basis to maintain dialogue

- Support in the preparation of transaction marketing and process materials including term sheets

- Process coordination from launch to signing, in close cooperation with other internal teams, including investor outreach, active communication with investors / management, and overall transaction management

- Analyse proposals received from investors including comparison of key terms and oversee financial modelling to analyse returns under different structures. Support in the final negotiations for transactions

- Support in preparation of materials to present to J.P. Morgan clients, in partnership with industry or country teams

- Given the team’s high deal flow and its flat hierarchical structure, you should expect to be asked to perform a great variety of tasks, including many opportunities to ‘step-up’

Required qualifications, capabilities and skills

- Several years of full time investment banking experience

- Keen interest in private capital markets, minority M&A, and structured transactions. Interest in how minority transactions work including shareholder and governance agreements.

- Desire to work across sectors and have exposure to lots of different types of transactions

- Strong technical ability and overall corporate finance proficiency. The role will require flexibility to work across the capital spectrum and be exposed to new and creative structures. In particular, it is important to be able to have an understanding of capital structures and investor returns modelling

- Ability to engage in client and investors communications

- Ability to take ownership across a transaction, with exposure to industry, country, and product teams

- Ability to show initiative and support across several transactions in parallel, managing time appropriately across competing demands

Preferred qualifications, capabilities and skills

- Prior experience in M&A or capital raising be it equity or debt / leveraged finance

- Prior experience in communicating with buyside investors

This role encompasses the performance of regulated activity. The successful candidate will therefore be subject to meeting regulatory requirements in the assessment of fitness, propriety, knowledge and competence (as assessed by the firm) and (where appropriate) approval by the relevant regulatory authorities to carry out such activities.


Opportunity to join the J.P. Morgan’s growing Private Capital M&A team (which sits within EMEA M&A and is part of the global Private Capital Advisory & Solutions team), which is originating and executing common equity and structured private capital transactions across sectors and regions in EMEA.

jobs.title: Investment Banking - EMEA Technology M&A - Analyst / Associate - London
jobs.description:
About the Team

J.P. Morgan advises corporations, institutions, and sponsors of all sizes on mergers and acquisitions, meeting the most complex strategic needs in local markets as well as on a global scale. Our EMEA Technology M&A team combines deep sector expertise with global connectivity to deliver outcomes that shape our clients' futures. This is an opportunity for a highly motivated individual to advise Technology clients on M&A transactions across EMEA.

Job Summary

As a member of the EMEA Technology M&A team, you will play a critical role in originating and executing M&A transactions, partnering closely with industry and country coverage teams and other product teams across the bank. Working alongside expert senior bankers, you will contribute to high-profile transactions from day one, developing strong functional skills across the major areas of investment banking.

Job Responsibilities

- Drive origination and execution of transactions from launch to signing, including preparation of marketing materials, financial modelling and analysis, due diligence review, and preparation of other transaction materials, working closely with both internal teams and external stakeholders

- Support origination by preparing pitch materials, screening potential targets, and monitoring sector developments and live situations

- Develop content for strategic client meetings on M&A transactions, including sell side, buy side, and defence mandates

- Perform detailed valuation analysis and model transaction structures, return profiles, and scenarios to assess optimal terms and economics for clients

- Design bespoke sale processes and support end-to-end transaction execution alongside internal partners and external advisers

- Prepare comprehensive client materials including pitch books, board presentations, business plans, due diligence outputs, and marketing documents

- Manage communication with clients, counterparties, and other advisers throughout the transaction process

- Take on significant responsibility due to the team's high deal flow and flat hierarchical structure

- Partner closely with JPM industry, country, and product teams to deliver integrated advice

- Maintain up-to-date knowledge of industry trends, transaction developments, and technology innovations

Your Growth at J.P. Morgan

JPM Tech M&A is a long-term career platform. Analysts and Associates benefit from:

- Structured training and development curriculum, complemented by continuous on-the-job learning from senior bankers

- Direct exposure to clients and senior stakeholders from day one

- Clear promotion pathway with strong internal mobility across verticals, geographies, and adjacent product areas

- Membership of a global M&A franchise, with opportunities to work on cross-border transactions alongside colleagues in the US, Asia, and LATAM

Required Qualifications, Capabilities and Skills

- Technology M&A experience is required

- Demonstrated technical ability and overall corporate finance proficiency

- University degree with a strong academic record; Finance, Accounting, Economics, or related quantitative fields preferred but not required

- Strong accounting, quantitative, and business writing skills

- Understanding of the M&A transaction cycle and process steps

- Ability to take ownership of transactions, with significant exposure to clients, other third-party advisers, and counterparties

- Strong communication skills, with the ability to interact effectively with senior professionals, clients, and stakeholders across other lines of business

- Detail-oriented, proactive, and able to manage time appropriately across competing demands, working effectively under pressure and to tight deadlines

- Self-directed, highly motivated, and able to work independently

- Strong team orientation, integrity, and client service mindset

Preferred Qualifications, Capabilities and Skills

- Prior internship or full-time experience in M&A, corporate finance, private equity, or a related field

- Demonstrated interest in and/or exposure to the technology sector

- Proficiency in a European language (in addition to English) is desirable but not mandatory

- Familiarity with AI and productivity tools, and the ability to leverage them thoughtfully to enhance, not replace, analytical judgement and commercial reasoning

Regulatory Note

This role encompasses the performance of regulated activity. The successful candidate will therefore be subject to meeting regulatory requirements in the assessment of fitness, propriety, knowledge, and competence (as assessed by the Firm) and (where appropriate) approval by the relevant regulatory authorities to carry out such activities.

jobs.title: 2027 Commercial & Investment Banking - Risk Management Program - Summer Internship - London
jobs.description:
Description

As an intern in the Commercial & Investment Banking Risk Management Program in London, you will work with industry experts to identify, assess and manage risk for our global businesses. You’ll collaborate with colleagues at all levels, gain broad product knowledge, build your network, and develop expertise in a diverse, supportive environment. We value your unique perspective to help us innovate for our clients and we will provide the tools to succeed with training and mentorship, and the chance to work on engaging projects.

Risk Management plays a critical role in helping the firm grow responsibly by identifying, assessing and managing risks across global markets and businesses. Join a collaborative environment where you'll gain valuable industry exposure, build meaningful relationships, and contribute to work that has real impact.

What You Can Expect

Understanding, mitigating and managing risk is central to the current and future success of our business. Our Risk managers shape decisions, influence models and interface with regulators to protect our financial reputation.

Program overview: Nine-weeks, with a five-day induction and training led by expert instructors and JPMorganChase professionals. You'll build your technical and practical knowledge on-the-job with opportunities in one of the chosen risk teams listed below:

- The Credit Risk Team  is responsible for reviewing client credit strength and approving and managing  retained credit risk (risk of default) within the Commercial and Investment Bank (CIB). Credit risk arises through underwriting, lending and trading activities, including investment and non-investment grade syndicated loans, acquisition finance, derivatives, foreign exchange and other products.

- The Market Risk Team partners closely with the CIB trading businesses to independently identify, measure, monitor, and report market risk across multiple asset classes (FX, Rates, Equities, Credit, Securitized Products, and Commodities). The team tracks market events, performs portfolio risk analytics, runs scenario analysis, sets risk limits and provides timely risk escalation as exposures evolve. Market Risk’s insights regularly inform senior management’s decisions on the firm’s risk appetite—particularly ahead of and during periods of elevated market volatility.

- The Chief Investment Office, Treasury and Corporate (CTC) Risk Team  is an independent risk function that manages the risk of the retained portfolio generated from the CTC businesses and includes Market Risk, Credit Risk, Reputational Risk, Country Risk, Principal Risk, and Model Risk.  CTC Risk is also responsible for the independent risk management of Firmwide Liquidity Risk, Interest Rate Risk, and Capital Risk.

This internship offers hands-on experience, targeted training, and valuable networking opportunities to advance your career. The program is based at JPMorganChase’s EMEA headquarters in London. Successful interns may receive full-time graduate program offers for the following year at their chosen location.

Job Responsibilities

- Learn risk management at a leading global bank

- Collaborate to solve complex problems

- Develop innovative solutions

- Manage relationships with clients, regulators, and stakeholders

- Understand the importance of integrity and transparency

Required qualifications, skills, and capabilities

- Analytical, quantitative, and project management skills

- Excellent written and verbal English communication

- Interest in global financial markets

- Energetic, confident, and adaptable in a fast-paced environment

- Ability to multitask and work under pressure

- Proficient in Microsoft Excel, Word, and PowerPoint

- Open to all degree disciplines

- Experience with Python or similar coding languages

- Demonstrable interest and achievements beyond academia showcasing the unique contribution you could bring to our team.

- Some teams may require language skills; please list your fluency on your application.

Expected graduation of January 2028 and September 2028

- Use a long-term email address (not .edu or .ac.uk).

- If successful you’ll progress to a Superday, further information will be provided

JPMorganChase is committed to creating an inclusive work environment that respects all people for their unique skills, backgrounds and experiences. We strive to hire qualified, diverse candidates, and we will provide accommodations for known disabilities.


Lead risk solutions, expand product expertise, and grow through training, mentorship, and impactful projects in a collaborative team.
