jobs.title: Compensation, Incentive Administration – Vice President
jobs.description:
JPMorgan Chase is seeking a Vice President to join our Compensation team!

As an Incentive Administration Vice President within our Compensation team, you will oversee the implementation, administration, governance and ongoing management of incentive compensation programs across Business Banking. You will support cross organization efforts with Consumer Bank at times and partner with Human Resources, Finance, Sales Strategy, Incentive Operations, Technology, Risk, Controls and business leaders to administer plans accurately, maintain effective governance and support business objectives. The role balances operational execution, implementation coordination and complex program administration, with a consistent focus on accuracy, controls, and continuous improvement.

Job Responsibilities:

- Administer incentive compensation programs and interpret plan provisions and administration guidelines; partner with Finance to validate incentive calculations, reporting outputs and payouts.

- Support participant eligibility reviews, plan documentation, governance activities and approved plan updates.

Bring your expertise to JPMorgan Chase. As part of Risk Management and Compliance, you are at the center of keeping JPMorgan Chase strong and resilient. As an Executive Director Technology Development Risk Lead in Technology and Cybersecurity Operational Risk Management, you form an independent view of whether the controls over software delivery still hold now that a large share of code is written by artificial intelligence agents. You will use data-first approaches to show what is actually happening across the engineering estate, challenge the first line on what that data reveals, and report a position that senior management and regulators can rely on. You will do this as an individual contributor, close enough to the technology to stay credible with the engineers you challenge.

Your role offers the opportunity to join the Tech and Cyber Operational Risk Management team, responsible for the successful implementation and execution of the Compliance, Conduct, and Operational Risk framework within JPMorgan. You will provide Second Line of Defense challenge and oversight to our technology and cybersecurity partners. We are looking for someone who has built software and can hold their own with the engineers they challenge, and who will raise the analytical bar of the people around them without managing them.

Job Responsibilities:

-
Perform independent risk assessments of the controls governing how software is planned, written, reviewed, tested, and released, using data-first approaches and advanced analytics.

-
Challenge the first line on the control model applied to artificial intelligence coding assistants and agentic development tooling, covering human review of generated code, attribution of authorship, and the audit trail behind every change.

-
Evaluate the entitlements and credentials granted to development tooling and autonomous agents, and whether access controls still hold when a machine rather than a person initiates a change.

-
Assess whether observability and telemetry across the engineering estate is sufficient to detect data loss, misuse, and unexpected agent behaviour.

-
Utilize Python and SQL to analyze large engineering data sets, and build dashboards and reports that make development risk visible to senior management.

-
Define and test statistical hypotheses to identify thematic risks in software delivery from key risk indicator and key performance indicator performance.

-
Develop and maintain the annual oversight plan for this domain, and report an independent view to senior management, control committees, internal audit, and regulators.

-
Assess the prioritization and treatment of control findings, and monitor first line remediation to closure.

-
Coach and develop junior data scientists and risk professionals, raising the analytical bar of the function.

Required Qualifications, Capabilities, and Skills:

-
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Information Security, or a related field, or equivalent experience.

-
15 years of experience in technology risk, technology audit, software engineering, or application security within financial services.

-
Hands-on software development experience in Python.

-
Experience querying and analyzing data in SQL.

-
Hands-on experience with the software delivery toolchain, including source control, continuous integration and delivery pipelines, and automated testing.

-
Experience assessing or testing technology controls such as change management, access management, or secure software development.

-
Experience with data visualization and reporting tools such as Tableau or AWS QuickSight.

-
Experience presenting technology risk findings to senior management.

-
Experience coaching or developing junior technical colleagues.

Preferred Qualifications, Capabilities, and Skills:

-
Hands-on experience with artificial intelligence coding assistants or agentic development tooling in a professional software delivery setting.

-
Experience with large language models, including prompt design and evaluation of model output.

-
Experience with observability and monitoring platforms such as Splunk, Datadog, or Dynatrace.

-
Experience with cloud platforms, container orchestration, or infrastructure as code.

-
A professional certification such as CISA, CISM, CISSP, or CRISC.

jobs.title: Risk Management & Compliance Governance Lead Vice President
jobs.description:
Description

Bring your expertise to JPMorgan Chase. As part of Risk Management and Compliance, you are at the center of keeping JPMorgan Chase strong and resilient. You help the firm grow its business in a responsible way by anticipating new and emerging risks, and using your expert judgement to solve real-world challenges that impact our company, customers and communities. Our culture in Risk Management and Compliance is all about thinking outside the box, challenging the status quo and striving to be best-in-class.

As a Vice President in the Credit Risk Governance team, you will collaborate with global Wealth Management functions, including Risk, Lending Solutions, Operations, Legal, and Compliance. Your role will involve working with the Wealth Management Risk function to develop and maintain policies, standards, guidelines, and procedures, including regulatory compliance measures. You will work closely with the Front Office to assess business needs and develop risk controls to achieve revenue targets and business growth. Your responsibilities will also include maintaining a full inventory of documents and ensuring they are clear, concise, and user-friendly. You will assist in developing and implementing the business risk management framework, including risk governance and controls, organization structure, policies and procedures, and risk measures and metrics. You will also be responsible for delivering large-scale risk and regulatory change and technical initiatives. Communication of changes, detailing requirements, and strategic risk management objectives to large working groups, including senior management, will be a key part of your role. You will also work with internal groups such as Credit, Investment, and Fiduciary Risk areas, as well as Compliance, Legal, and Operations on matters related to risk controls, model-assessments, incidents, and infrastructure projects. Lastly, you will provide support and guidance for audits and regulatory examinations.

Job Responsibilities

- Work with  Wealth Management Risk function to develop and maintain policies, standards, guidelines, and procedures, including regulatory compliance measures and risk advisory within the Risk Management Program.

- Work closely with the Front Office to assess business needs and further develop risk controls to efficiently achieve revenue target and new business growth.

- Play a key role in the hierarchy and design of documentation by maintaining full inventory of documents.

- Review documentation to ensure it is clear, concise, and user-friendly. Perform ongoing updates to existing documentation to ensure they remain accurate and relevant.

- Assist in developing, design, implementation, and support of line of business risk management framework, including but not limited to: Risk governance and controls, organization structure, policies and procedures, three lines of defense, risk measures and metrics (risk appetite and limits, monitoring and escalation).

- Deliver large-scale risk and regulatory change and technical initiatives.

- Communicate changes including detailing requirements and strategic risk management objectives/updates to large working groups, including senior management.

- Work alongside internal groups such as Credit, Investment, and Fiduciary Risk areas as well as Compliance, Legal, and Operations on matters related to risk controls, model-assessments, incidents, and infrastructure projects.

- Provide support and guidance for audits and regulatory examinations.

Required qualifications, capabilities, and skills

- Bachelor's Degree or commensurate related job experience

- 5+ years of experience in Auditing, Accounting, Internal Control and/or Credit Analysis with focus on Wholesale Credit Risk

- Strong business writing skills

- Experience in Wholesale Audit, Compliance, Operational, and/or Regulatory Risk Management

- Demonstrated ability to collaborate cross-functions to achieve measurable results

- Strong organizational skills

- Ability to manage and prioritize multiple requests at the same time

- Detail oriented with strong analytical skills

- Proficiency in Microsoft Word, Excel, and PowerPoint

Preferred qualifications, capabilities, and skills

- Project and/or Change Management experience preferred


The position will include proactive management of credit risk policies, guidelines, and procedures.

jobs.title: Risk Management - Stress Testing - Senior Associate
jobs.description:
Join JPMorgan Chase and help strengthen how the firm identifies, measures, and manages operational risk. As part of the Operational Risk team, you’ll apply quantitative expertise, analytical judgment, and innovative thinking to support scenario analysis activities that inform risk management, stress testing, and senior-level decision-making.
As a Stress Testing Senior Officer – Senior Associate in the Firmwide Risk and Compliance team, you will support the development of risk estimation methodologies and the execution of Operational Risk Scenario Analysis activities. You will work closely with senior executives, subject matter experts, Risk Identification leads across Lines of Business, Operational Risk Officers, Model Risk, and Legal partners to structure scenarios, estimate risk drivers, assess potential outcomes, and enhance analytical tools and models.

Job responsibilities:
- Support development and enhancement of Operational Risk Scenario Analysis quantification methodologies.
- Structure operational risk scenarios and estimate key risk drivers, including exposure, impact, and occurrence.
- Facilitate Presentations
- Conduct data-driven and subject matter expert-based analysis to assess scenario outcomes.
- Partner with Lines of Business, Risk Identification teams, Operational Risk Officers, Model Risk, Legal, and other stakeholders to gather inputs and challenge assumptions.
- Support model risk activities, including documentation, validation reviews, issue remediation, and governance.
- Develop and enhance analytical tools, estimation approaches, and models for Scenario Analysis, CCAR, DFAST, and ICAAP stress testing.
- Perform data analysis, sensitivity analysis, benchmarking, back-testing, and output reasonableness assessments.
- Explore machine learning and GenAI-enabled approaches for scenario analysis, risk taxonomy, and unstructured data use cases.
- Identify opportunities to automate workflows, improve scalability, strengthen controls, and enhance transparency.
- Translate complex quantitative, technical, and risk concepts into clear insights for senior stakeholders.

Required qualifications, capabilities, and skills:
- Bachelor’s degree in a quantitative, analytical, technical, financial, or related discipline.
- Proven experience facilitating Presentations
- Proven background in Coding
- 3 years plus of experience in data analytics, quantitative analysis, model development, risk analytics, operational risk, stress testing, or a related field; or advanced degree with 2 years of relevant experience.
- Strong analytical, quantitative, and problem-solving skills, with intellectual curiosity and sound business judgment.


Help evolve operational risk estimation through quantitative methodology, model development, automation, and data-driven insights.

jobs.title: Risk Management - Stress Testing - Executive Director
jobs.description:
Bring your Expertise to JPMorganChase. As part of Risk Management and Compliance, you are at the center of keeping JPMorganChase strong and resilient. You help the firm grow its business in a responsible way by anticipating new and emerging risks, and using your expert judgement to solve real-world challenges that impact our company, customers and communities. Our culture in Risk Management and Compliance is all about thinking outside the box, challenging the status quo and striving to be best-in-class.

As an Executive Director in the Loan Loss Forecasting team, you will lead the Commercial and Industrial (C&I) Portfolio team based in Plano and shape the integrity and quality of the firm’s wholesale credit loan loss estimates. You provide portfolio-level monitoring and guidance across a diverse C&I exposure base, supporting stress testing, allowance estimation, and methodology development. You collaborate with senior executives and partners across Risk, Finance, Treasury, Controllers, and Quantitative Research to deliver high-quality analytics and insights. You help us inform firmwide risk and finance programs, including CECL (Current Expected Credit Loss), IFRS 9 (International Financial Reporting Standard 9), quarterly stress testing, and CCAR (Comprehensive Capital Analysis and Review).

Job responsibilities:

- Oversee C&I exposure at a portfolio level across held-for-investment (HFI) and fair value option (FVO), monitoring trends and estimating impacts to allowance and limits for large deals

- Review top-level and loan-level allowance and stress testing results for reasonability, accuracy, and alignment with portfolio trends

- Assess risks and support estimation of qualitative loan loss reserves, incorporating management judgment, industry data, and emerging or idiosyncratic risk factors

- Calculate, analyze, and communicate key modeling parameters, including probability of default, loss given default, exposure at default, and rating migration, and translate them into actionable loss estimates

- Develop and deepen expertise in allowance and stress testing estimation processes, informing methodology across CECL and CCAR forecasting exercises

- Lead portfolio trend and sensitivity analyses across macroeconomic scenarios, portfolio stress tests, and assumption changes to support strategic decision-making

- Support monitoring of monthly stress testing output across scenarios and coordinate limit usage reviews with Credit Officers

- Provide stress estimates for large and complex deals and run ad-hoc scenarios for senior management based on market conditions

Required qualifications, capabilities, and skills:

- Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Business, Finance, Accounting, or a related quantitative field

- 8 years plus of experience in the financial services industry, and/or in the banking sector

- Strong familiarity with credit products

- Knowledge of CECL credit loss accounting standards

- Knowledge of the CCAR regulatory framework and stress testing requirements

- Demonstrated ability to collaborate across diverse groups, build consensus, and execute plans while managing multiple concurrent workstreams

- Strong oral and written communication skills, including distilling complex topics into clear messaging for senior management

- Proficiency in Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint, and other Office applications

- Experience with data analysis and manipulation using analytical tools such as Tableau, Python, or Alteryx, including use of large language models


Promote risk strategy by anticipating threats, challenging assumptions, and guiding responsible growth for the firm.

jobs.title: Data Product & Governance Lead Vice President
jobs.description:
You help JPMorganChase grow its business in a responsible way by anticipating new and emerging risks and using your expert judgement to solve real-world challenges that impact our company, customers and communities. As the Data Governance & Data Product Lead in the Office of Regulation and Document Governance (ORDG), you will own the foundation layer of ORDG’s Data, Analytics & AI capability — turning policy content into governed, machine-readable data products that AI services, controls and reporting all consume. Reporting to ORDG’s Executive Data Owner, you will define and run the data-product operating model: standards, taxonomy, ownership, quality gates, certification, and lifecycle. Partnering with Technology, Data Science, Product Owners and the wider RM&C community, you will ensure the governed data foundation is trusted, reusable and defensible — so that every downstream AI capability, dashboard and control across FPSP, DOGMA, LRCM and the RM&C Bulletin Tool operates on the same authoritative source of truth.

- Establish and enforce quality gates and controls across the data foundation — completeness, conformance, KDE integrity, lineage traceability, and normativity separation — partnering with the Data Quality & Controls function on measurement and remediation.

- Partner with Technology to translate governance intent into implemented physical data models, contracts and consumption interfaces across the governed data-product estate.

- Represent ORDG in firmwide data governance forums, contributing to and drawing from broader JPMorganChase data standards, taxonomies and controls.

- Deep expertise in data-product design principles — canonical models, data contracts, Key Data Elements, taxonomy management, lineage and quality frameworks.

Maintain a strong control environment by ensuring procedures and desk instructions are current; reviews and approvals are evidenced; records are complete; and activities remain audit-ready.

-
Monitor key deliverables, aging items, recurring defects, and emerging risks; provide concise management reporting and ensure timely corrective action.

-
Drive process improvements through standardization, workflow enhancements, automation opportunities, stronger reconciliations, and improved exception visibility.

-
Partner effectively with Operations, Asset Management, Risk, Finance, Legal, Technology, Agency partners, vendors, and other stakeholders to support compliant and resilient servicing execution.

-
Promote a culture of accountability, sound judgment, constructive challenge, continuous learning, and best-in-class borrower and client service.

-
At least 5 years of combined experience in multifamily mortgage loan insurance compliance, escrow administration, and tax servicing.

-
Prior experience leading others through direct people management or demonstrated team leadership, including coaching, training, workflow oversight, review or quality assurance accountability, or acting-lead responsibilities.

-
Working familiarity with Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac multifamily servicing and insurance requirements, with the ability to interpret and apply program guides, coverage standards, and servicing obligations.

-
Knowledge of commercial property and casualty insurance, including property, flood, wind, earthquake, terrorism, general liability, workers compensation, automobile, professional liability, and umbrella or excess coverage.

-
Working knowledge of real estate tax administration, escrow account reconciliation, escrow analysis methodologies, shortage and surplus calculations, borrower payment adjustments, and exception resolution.

-
Strong control mindset and attention to detail, with the ability to maintain complete documentation, identify emerging risks, and make sound decisions with limited supervision.

-
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to coach employees, set clear expectations, influence stakeholders, and communicate complex issues to leadership.

-
Ability to manage competing priorities, deadlines, vendors, and escalations in a fast-paced environment while maintaining consistent execution and service quality.

-
Strong Microsoft Office proficiency, particularly Excel, Word, Outlook, and PowerPoint.

Preferred Qualifications, Capabilities and Skills

-
Bachelor’s degree in Business, Finance, Accounting, Risk Management, Insurance, or equivalent work experience.

-
Experience working with third-party insurance and tax service providers, including vendor output review, issue reconciliation, performance oversight, and escalation management.

-
Experience reviewing commercial insurance policies, binders, endorsements, certificates, and evidence of insurance for compliance with Agency and lender requirements.

-
Knowledge of commercial real estate loan documents as they relate to insurance, taxes, escrow obligations, lender protections, and borrower servicing requirements.

-
Experience with McCracken Strategy and insurance or tax monitoring platforms.

-
Experience developing procedures, training materials, quality review routines, management reporting, and leadership-ready summaries.


Lead a team responsible for insurance compliance, real estate tax administration, and escrow analysis.
